transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-02-25
Time: 15:00 PST
Duration: ~65 minutes
Attendees: Sophie (PM), Arjun (Eng Lead), Maya (TPM), Daniel (SRE), Olivia (Prod Ops), Kevin (QA)

Summary:
Quick handoff from Q2 roadmap work into Q3 launch readiness for the upcoming Redwood Hosted performance improvements and Dedicated cluster rollout. Reviewed recent incident, outstanding tech debt, perf numbers, and canary/rollback criteria. Agreed on concrete next steps and owners.

Topics:
- Incident review from 2026-02-18 outage
- Performance benchmarks (95th p latency, cost per token)
- Launch readiness checklist (dry run dates, stakeholders)
- Rollout plan: canary thresholds, autoscale limits, fallback models
- Open action items and owner alignment

Action items (see metadata): listed during meeting

Transcript:
[00:00:03] Sophie: okay, uh let's get started, thanks everyone for joining on short notice, I think we've got 65 minutes on the calendar so we'll run through the RCA, perf numbers and then the launch checklist, quick round robin intros if someone new, Kevin from QA is here to talk regression plans.

[00:00:18] Arjun: hey everyone, Arjun here, I'll cover the perf runs and the cluster ramps, also some notes on quantization regressions we saw in staging.

[00:00:25] Maya: Maya TPM, I'll keep the timeline and rollout artefacts in sync, and will own dry-run coordination.

[00:00:30] Daniel: Daniel SRE, I'll cover the incident summary and mitigations.

[00:00:36] Olivia: Olivia product ops, I'll take notes on comms and support handoffs.

[00:01:02] Sophie: cool, quick context - our Q3 goal is to GA the new batching + prefetch caching improvements for Hosted and to enable Dedicated customers to opt into the new kernel selection path. We committed to an SLA-ish target of 95th percentile latency under 350ms for standard prompts for the hosted tier, and to keep unit cost within the target. so we need to align on what counts as ready.

[00:02:10] Daniel: i'll start with the incident from 18th, summary - at 02:14 UTC we saw a cascading capacity overload on a subset of Dedicated nodes after a kernel fallback path caused evictions in the KV cache, which increased CPU and memory pressure, autoscaler then spun up new pods, which actually temporarily increased load and hit the rate-limiter threshold. The immediate cause was a bad kernel selector edge case for long-context streams, plus a too-aggressive prefetch loop.

[00:03:05] Sophie: just to clarify, that was the fallback to the older kernel, right, not a completely different model?

[00:03:12] Daniel: right, it fell back from the optimized kernel to the compatibility kernel which wasn't respecting our continuous-batching memory accounting; kv cache eviction and prefetch compounding.

[00:03:35] Arjun: and to be clear we've seen similar patterns in staging when sequence lengths spike; we added a guard but the edge-case in the selector wasn't triggered in the unit tests. so lesson is we need more production-esque sequences in benchmarks, including long chained dialogues and function-calling outputs.

[00:04:05] Kevin: QA noticed a slight difference in output tokens after the quantization profile changed, some mis-tokenization leading to slower per-token generation on certain prompts. might be related?

[00:04:20] Arjun: possible, the quantization and kernel choice interact, especially with KV cache layout. i'll include checks.

[00:05:00] Maya: okay, RCA and immediate mitigations?

[00:05:07] Daniel: immediate mitigation was to push a temporary config that disabled aggressive prefetch and force the older behavior on the affected pool while we rolled back the kernel selector patch. medium term, we plan to add a canary policy that restricts fallback frequency and forces a per-node memory accounting sample. long term, update selector tests and add production-like workloads to the perf suite.

[00:06:22] Sophia: (interruption) sorry sophie, small note - do we have a timeline for the mitigation rollouts?

[00:06:30] Daniel: we pushed the temporary config within 40 minutes of detection. full selector fix is targeted for next sprint, but we should include a hotfix path if needed.

[00:07:00] Sophie: okay thanks. Arjun can you run the perf slate and include long-context sequences and function-call heavy payloads? we need 95th p numbers and cost per token numbers with and without KV cache.

[00:07:20] Arjun: yes, plan is to run dedicated cluster perf: baseline on current kernel, then optimized kernel with caching enabled, then with quantized model. i'll try to produce CSV with the 50/95/99 percentiles and cost calculations. note: staging results were promising but we need full production-like load to see autoscaler interactions.

[00:08:05] Kevin: for QA we'll add a regression set that includes long dialogues and prompt engineering edge-cases, also include some postprocessing verification for function calling outputs - sometimes the punctuation and casing changes and test assertions fail.

[00:09:12] Maya: timeline wise, dry-run week is penciled for 2026-03-08 to 2026-03-12. we need final signoffs by 2026-03-05 so that we can do a full sim during the dry run and hit GA in the week of 2026-03-22 if all goes well.

[00:09:45] Olivia: stakeholders to notify: Sales, Support, Legal (for SLA language), and two pilot customers (list in the drive). i'll prepare comms and the 24-hour escalation playbook.

[00:10:10] Sophie: good. now let's go through the launch readiness checklist quickly - can we call out items that are blocked?

[00:10:25] Arjun: blocked items: final perf numbers, stress test on Dedicated with mixed-model load, and a regression found in quantized path for small token sequences.

[00:10:40] Daniel: operational blockers: autoscaler tuning for the dedicated pools, and alert thresholds for memory pressure need review. current alerts are too noisy and caused paging in the last incident.

[00:11:05] Kevin: QA blockers: we need the release candidate image in the test harness, and the test infra needs to support the new kernel selection environment var toggles.

[00:11:20] Maya: okay, so owners: Arjun on perf runs and fix, Daniel on ops tuning and alerts, Kevin on QA gating, Sophie on stakeholder signoff and decisioning, Olivia on comms.

[00:12:00] Sophie: on rollout policy - propose canary 5% of traffic for 24 hours, then 25% for 12 hours, then full. rollback criteria: 95th p latency increase > 15% from baseline, or error rate increase > 0.5% absolute, or any unhandled OOM/eviction events. thoughts?

[00:12:35] Arjun: those thresholds sound reasonable, maybe tighten to 10% latency if we have accurate baselines. also we need an automated rollback if we see continuous eviction events for longer than 10 minutes.

[00:13:05] Daniel: agree, add eviction events condition and a memory-accounting alert that triggers a scale-in delay. Also make sure the fallback model variant is warm in the other region to avoid cross-region cold-starts during fallback.

[00:13:40] Olivia: for support we need a one-pager on troubleshooting steps for frontline, and we need a runbook link in the console.

[00:14:00] Sophie: noted. on monitoring - token-level cost breakdown needs to be enabled for the canary routes so product can see economics in real time. who's owning that?

[00:14:12] Arjun: infra can add route-level cost tagging, but I'll need Product's list of test prompts to compute per-token costs aligned to expected usage.

[00:14:38] Sophie: i'll provide the prompt set. Kevin, will QA include those?

[00:14:45] Kevin: yes, add to the regression harness. we'll run them in nightly and during dry-run.

[00:15:10] Maya: about dry-run - propose we simulate both spike traffic and tail-latency scenarios. Daniel you and Arjun should run an outage simulation where we force fallback frequency and observe autoscaler behavior.

[00:15:33] Daniel: yeah we can do that, i'll kick off a chaos test in staging and simulate heavy long-context concurrent sessions.

[00:16:05] Sophie: any concerns about compliance or audit logs for customers? remember Private customers will ask for audit retention > 12 months.

[00:16:20] Olivia: Legal flagged that we need to confirm KMS integration for Dedicated customers and to share SOC2 updates in the pilot docs. i'll loop in Security.

[00:16:40] Arjun: on the quantization regressions - i suspect our 8-bit profile is causing token alignment shifts for some tokenizers; we'll run a token-by-token diff and maybe ship a tokenizer patch or adjust quantization thresholds.

[00:17:02] Kevin: when you say token-by-token diff, note that tokenizers differ across model families, so tests must be model-specific. we should map prompts to model families in the test matrix.

[00:17:35] Sophie: good. can we talk about cost targets? finance expects unit token cost not to exceed X for GA - we need to provide scenarios for Hosted vs Dedicated.

[00:17:50] Arjun: i'll produce cost scenarios: baseline (no caching), caching enabled, and caching+quantization. will include assumptions: average prompt length, response length, and hit rate for prefix cache.

[00:18:15] Maya: also include network egress assumptions because some customers in APAC will ping regional infra and that affects cost.

[00:18:30] Sophie: okay. switching to stakeholder approvals - who needs to sign off from Product and GTM?

[00:18:37] Olivia: Sales leadership (Marta), Support lead (Jules), Privacy and Security (Anya), and Finance (Ravi) - I'll schedule the readout on 2026-03-05.

[00:19:05] Sophie: great. Any other technical risks we haven't discussed?

[00:19:20] Arjun: one more - the kernel selection code path had limited visibility in tracing. we need more detailed tracing around cache hits/evictions and kernel fallback events. this will help debug in future incidents.

[00:19:40] Daniel: agreed, add trace correlation id for eviction events and include pod metadata in logs. also crop the log volume for routine ops so we can keep the retention window manageable.

[00:20:10] Kevin: small note - in recent customer demo we saw a small prompt where function calling flattened arrays differently across kernels, we should include that scenario in the functional tests.

[00:20:30] Sophie: noted. okay, let's do a rapid-fire run through the remaining checklist items: metrics dashboard updates, runbook, QA gating, perf runs, dry-run scheduling, stakeholder signoff. call out blockers again.

[00:20:50] Maya: metrics dashboard - Arjun to add route-level cost, Daniel to add eviction and memory alerts, Olivia to create the support one-pager.

[00:21:10] Arjun: perf runs - I'll queue the dedicated cluster runs tonight, expect initial CSV by 2026-03-01. I'll include scenarios: 1) baseline, 2) cache enabled, 3) quantized.

[00:21:25] Daniel: SRE will update alerts and run chaos sim by 2026-03-02.

[00:21:36] Kevin: QA will run nightly regression and a pre-dry-run smoke by 2026-03-07.

[00:21:45] Olivia: comms drafted by 2026-02-27 for review.

[00:22:00] Sophie: good. any objections to the canary plan?

[00:22:06] Arjun: none from Eng.

[00:22:10] Daniel: none from SRE.

[00:22:15] Kevin: none from QA.

[00:22:20] Maya: okay, two quick operational questions - first, do we have capacity reservations in the Dedicated pool for the canary so pilot customers don't run into cold-starts? second, are we comfortable with regional fallbacks?

[00:22:38] Arjun: capacity reservation - we can reserve a small pool for canary traffic, but that increases cost. recommend reserve min nodes equal to expected baseline + 10% to avoid scale spikes. regional fallback - we should avoid cross-region fallback for latency-sensitive customers; fallback should be same-region model variant where possible.

[00:23:05] Olivia: i'll mark cost implications for reservations in the comms doc.

[00:23:20] Sophie: final section - decision log: we agree to proceed with the planned canary thresholds, run the perf suites, and do the dry-run week 2026-03-08. blockers must be resolved by 2026-03-05 or we delay. owners are captured in action items.

[00:23:45] Maya: anything else?

[00:23:50] Kevin: quick note: make sure we capture the exact test harness versions used in perf runs to avoid confusion later.

[00:24:05] Arjun: will annotate CSV with harness commit tag.

[00:24:20] Daniel: i'll add the incident timeline and a short list of mitigations to the RCA doc and post to the incident channel.

[00:24:35] Sophie: great. last thing - can we confirm next check-in for 2026-03-03 at 10am PST to review perf results and launch checklist?

[00:24:50] Maya: confirm.

[00:25:10] Olivia: confirmed for me.

[00:25:25] Kevin: same.

[00:25:45] Sophie: thanks everyone, i'll follow up with the doc links and a short recording. end.

[00:26:00] [end of recording]
